compare.title: How QuietJar compares.
compare.intro: Every tool here does something well. The question is what happens to your visitor after they decide to support you.

sections.name: Ko-fi
sections.text: Ko-fi charges 5% on tips by default, and only waives it on a paid Gold plan (checked September 2026). Your visitor clicks your button, lands on Ko-fi's page, and pays there with PayPal or a card. How many of them finish the trip?

sections.name: Buy Me a Coffee
sections.text: Buy Me a Coffee has the friendliest brand in the space and a huge installed base on blogs and READMEs. It takes a flat 5% platform fee with no cap (checked September 2026), and payment happens on its page, not yours. Does a coffee cup fit your site, and how many of your visitors finish the trip?

sections.name: Stripe direct
sections.text: Stripe is the best payment infrastructure there is, and you can build the button yourself on it: 1.5% + €0.25 per EU card and €0.29 per iDEAL payment (checked September 2026). Payment Links redirect to Stripe's page; Embedded Checkout stays on yours and needs real code. How many weekends, and who maintains it after?

sections.name: GitHub Sponsors
sections.text: GitHub Sponsors is the right default for maintainers, and it takes 0% (checked September 2026). It lives on github.com, both sides need a GitHub account, and support is recurring by default. How many of your readers ever open the repo? Use both.
